subject: USAGE BINARY-CHAR, BINARY-SHORT, BINARY-LONG, BINARY-DOUBLE (allow wider range than minimum specified)
notes: OWNER DECISION Q30, 2026-09-09 (kb/Work PB592), verbatim: "provided, the native range." It REPLACES the premise this row previously closed on. The row carried DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT through the `a1-optional-not-provided` derived selector (kb/Work PB280 Q1) because docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 7 said "Not provided. Each usage holds exactly the GR12 minimum range for its width" - and that determination was FALSE for all four SIGNED usages. 13.18.60.4 GR12's printed table is ASYMMETRIC and the asymmetry is the whole content of the rule: every SIGNED row prints a STRICT '<' on BOTH sides (-128 [-2**7] < n < 128 [2**7]) while every UNSIGNED row prints '<=' on the left (0 <= n < 256 [2**8]) - re-rendered from the canonical PDF for this landing (printed page 507), independently of the reading the note inherited. So the minimum SIGNED band EXCLUDES -2**(w-1), which this compiler stores; 15.58.4's NOTE concedes the same thing from inside the standard ("BINARY-CHAR SIGNED | -128 (assuming an 8-bit twos-complement representation)"). The optional element of A.1 item 206 - "allow wider range than minimum specified" - is therefore PROVIDED, by exactly one value per signed usage, and A.1's preamble ("Documentation required: If the element is provided by the implementor, the implementor's user documentation shall document the element ...", cite.py --check A.1 OK) read with 4.2.5 (the conformance clause that governs the A.1 list, cite.py --check OK) makes documenting it an obligation rather than an option. NOTE the ground named here is 4.2.5, NOT 4.2.7: 4.2.7's own first sentence scopes it to A.4 (kb/Work PB593). THE DETERMINATION, stated structurally here and ENUMERATED ONCE in the row's own register anchor (docs/CONFORMANCE.md#DOC-A.1-206, which the code-location above names): the full native two's-complement band of each usage's byte width - so each SIGNED usage expresses exactly ONE value beyond the GR12 minimum and the four UNSIGNED usages are exactly the minimum. The band is written down ONCE, as the byte width per usage (PicInfo.StorageWidth, 1/2/4/8) under the BinaryCapacity discipline (PicInfo.Truncation), and read by the runtime store bound (CobolNum.InBinaryRange / TryStoreU) and the compile-time HIGHEST/LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC fold (IntrinsicBinder.BindAlgebraicFold), which AlgebraicFoldContainerAgreementTests holds in agreement - which is why the two sites named above are the whole implementation and not a sample. WITNESS conformance:cases/A.1-Implementor-defined-language-element-list/pb592_binary_usage_range_bounds measures all three claims at the introducing edition: Part A round-trips both endpoints of all EIGHT GR12 minimum bands (0 included, since the unsigned bands are CLOSED at 0); Part B measures GR12's nesting sentence at BOTH extremes of each narrower signed usage through FUNCTION LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC (15.58.1) and FUNCTION HIGHEST-ALGEBRAIC (15.43.1), the leg the wider signed band actually puts at risk; Part C measures both edges of all eight PROVIDED bands and one step beyond each, reading its disposition from 14.7.5 (case 3 and GR2 make an ON SIZE ERROR firing mean "not expressible in this usage") and reporting, for the four unsigned -1 legs, WHICH value landed - the magnitude, per 14.9.25.4 GR6 d)2.b. No compiler change was needed: every edge already behaved as the documented band, measured on this tree at --std 2002 and --std 2023.
